assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Real image
items.clue: An image formed where rays of light actually meet.

items.label: Convex lens
items.clue: A lens that is thicker in the middle than at its edges.

items.label: Concave lens
items.clue: A lens that is thinner in the middle than at its edges.

items.label: Virtual image
items.clue: An image formed where rays of light only appear to come from.

questions.stem: Rays of light travelling parallel to the principal axis pass into a convex lens. What happens to these rays?

options.text: They are refracted and brought to a focus at the principal focus
They are reflected from the front face of the lens to a point
They are refracted and cross each other at the focal length
They pass straight through and bend only as they leave

questions.explanation: This is what the specification states: in a convex lens, parallel rays of light are brought to a focus at the principal focus.

questions.stem: What is meant by the focal length of a convex lens?

options.text: The distance from the lens to the object being viewed
The distance from the lens to the principal focus
The distance from the lens to the sharp image
The thickness of the lens where it is widest

questions.explanation: This is the specification's definition: the distance from the lens to the principal focus is called the focal length.

questions.stem: A convex lens forms an image of a distant tree on a screen. Where does the light change direction?

options.text: Only at the surface where the light leaves the lens
At the shiny front face, where light is reflected
As it enters the lens and again as it leaves
Only at the middle, where it is thickest

questions.explanation: A lens has two surfaces and refraction happens at both, which together bring the parallel rays from the tree to a focus.

questions.stem: Which statement about the image formed by a concave lens is always true?

options.text: It is real if the object is far enough away
It is inverted, like the image from a lens
It is too faint for anyone to look at it
It is virtual, wherever the object is

questions.explanation: The specification states that the image produced by a concave lens is always virtual, whatever the object distance.

questions.stem: An object is placed between a convex lens and its principal focus, as in a magnifying glass. What sort of image is formed?

options.text: A real image, inverted and larger than the object
A virtual image, upright and larger than the object
A virtual image, upright but smaller than it
A real image formed at the principal focus

questions.explanation: Inside the principal focus the rays leaving the lens are still diverging, so the image is virtual, upright and magnified.

questions.stem: How can you tell that an image formed by a lens is real rather than virtual?

options.text: It appears the same way up as the object does
It can be seen by looking through the lens
It can be caught on a screen put where it forms
It is on the same side of the lens as the object

questions.explanation: A real image is formed where rays of light actually meet, so a screen placed there shows it.

questions.stem: In a ray diagram for a convex lens, how is the ray from the top of the object to the centre of the lens drawn?

options.text: It is bent so that it passes through the principal focus
It is curved to follow the two faces of the lens
It is bent back to run parallel to the principal axis
It carries straight on, with no change of direction

questions.explanation: At the centre the faces of the lens are effectively parallel, so the ray emerges travelling in its original direction.

questions.stem: In a ray diagram for a concave lens, a ray arrives parallel to the principal axis. How is it drawn after the lens?

options.text: Spreading away from the principal axis
Bending in to reach the principal focus beyond
Carrying straight on to the far side of it
Bending inwards to cross the principal axis

questions.explanation: A concave lens diverges the light, and only the line traced backwards passes through the principal focus.

questions.stem: A student draws ray diagrams for a convex lens and for a concave lens, using the same object in each. Which feature is the same in both diagrams?

options.text: Both images are turned upside down compared with the object
Both images can be caught on a screen behind
The ray through the centre of the lens is undeviated
The parallel ray goes to the focus beyond the lens

questions.explanation: This construction rule is shared by both lenses, and is one of the similarities a comparison of the diagrams should bring out.

questions.stem: Which two quantities are needed to calculate the magnification produced by a lens?

options.text: The focal length of the lens and the object height
The distance to the image and to the object
The height of the image and the focal length
The height of the image and the object height

questions.explanation: The specification gives magnification = (image height)/(object height), so the two heights are what is needed.

questions.stem: An object 5 mm tall produces an image 15 mm tall. What is the magnification?

options.text: 3, from 15 mm divided by 5 mm
0.33, from 5 mm divided by 15 mm
3 mm, as the heights were in mm
10, from 15 mm minus 5 mm

questions.explanation: magnification = (image height)/(object height) = 15/5 = 3, written as a plain number.

questions.stem: An object 8.0 cm tall produces an image 2.4 cm tall. What is the magnification?

options.text: 3.3, since 8.0 is divided by 2.4
0.30, as the image is smaller
3.3, because a lens should enlarge
0.30 cm, from the heights in cm

questions.explanation: magnification = (image height)/(object height) = 2.4/8.0 = 0.30, a value less than 1 because the image is diminished.
